name: iopl
description: iopl() changes the I/O privilege level of the calling thread based on the two least significant bits in the level parameter. It is deprecated, slower than ioperm(2), and primarily used for the i386 architecture on Linux.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Specifies the new I/O privilege level using the two least significant bits; the level for a normal thread is 0.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The calling thread has insufficient privilege; the CAP_SYS_RAWIO capability is required.

bugs: This call is deprecated and significantly slower than ioperm(2), intended only for older X servers requiring access to all 65536 I/O ports. Prior to Linux 5.5, it could disable interrupts and crash the system. Prior to Linux 3.7, permissions were inherited by child processes via fork(2) and preserved across execve(2), but this behavior changed.
versions: glibc2; with changes in Linux 3.7 and 5.5
